candidates.content_text:
Location: Rockhampton
Remuneration/Benefit: Competitive remuneration including overtime. Relocation packages available.
About the role:
Aurizon Network Asset Management is looking for a motivated Civil / Structural Engineer to join our Civil and Structures Assets team and help shape the future of one of Australia’s most important rail networks.
You will contribute to the asset management strategy that connects inland producers with ports along the Queensland coast, from Bowen through Sarina to Gladstone. This is a broad, hands-on role offering exposure to the full asset lifecycle—from understanding asset condition and risk through to shaping renewal scopes, budgets, designs and delivery priorities.
You will help develop capital renewal and maintenance programs across a diverse civil and structures portfolio, including:
- Structures — more than 4,000 culverts, 300 bridges, retaining walls and other structural assets
- Level crossings — more than 700 crossings with a mix of active and passive controls
- Geotechnical and earthworks — steep slopes through several mountain ranges and the formation supporting the track asset
- Access points and access roads — connecting our teams safely and efficiently with railway infrastructure
- Corridor security and fencing — supporting a rail network across an area larger than Tasmania
Working closely with Design Management, Program Management, operations and maintenance teams, you will influence practical, whole-of-business outcomes from concept and design through to delivery of renewal works—balancing safety, risk, track access, cost and scope.
- Influence stakeholders across the business to achieve better outcomes for civil and structures assets
- Assess asset condition, defects and failure modes, applying risk-based engineering judgement to support investment decisions
- Develop renewal and maintenance scopes, budgets and forward programs, and manage changes through planning and delivery
- Improve the processes, tools and data used to make asset management decisions
- Develop and refine strategies, standards, policies and practical engineering guidelines
- Analyse asset information and translate it into clear priorities and recommendations
Around 20% of your time will be spent in the field travelling across the network, giving you direct exposure to the assets you manage and the people who operate and maintain them. The balance offers flexible working across the office and home.
About you:
You are an early-to-mid career Civil or Structural Engineer who is ready to broaden your experience beyond a single project or discipline. You bring experience in design, construction and/or asset management, and you are keen to apply your technical knowledge in a practical operational environment. You enjoy solving complex problems, learning from experienced professionals and working with a wide range of stakeholders to turn sound engineering into real-world outcomes.
Qualifications and experience:
- Bachelor of Civil Engineering or equivalent (mandatory)
- Approximately 2–8 years’ experience in a civil or structural engineering role (mandatory)
- The ability to obtain registration a Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ) in the next 2 years (preferred)
- Experience with rail track infrastructure (desirable, but not essential)
What you will bring:
- A practical understanding of infrastructure operations, design, construction, maintenance and safety requirements
- Clear communication skills and the confidence to consult, negotiate and influence at different levels of the business
- The ability to apply legislation, regulation, standards and engineering requirements in a practical and proportionate way
- Strong written communication skills, with an interest in developing standards, specifications, policies, guidelines and processes
- Commercial awareness and the ability to balance risk, performance, cost and deliverability
If you are ready to accelerate your development, take ownership of a diverse infrastructure portfolio and see the impact of your decisions in the field, we would like to hear from you.
What we offer you:             
At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.
- Parental leave program and super booster.
About Aurizon.
Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets. 
Look to Aurizon for a diverse and collaborative culture.
At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.
To learn about us and our company values, please visit www.aurizon.com.au/careers

candidates.content_text:
Estimator – Commercial Partitions, Ceilings & Fit-Out
Total Trade Constructions | Croydon, Melbourne VIC
Full-Time | Permanent | Salary 
Know your way around steel stud framing, plasterboard, ceilings, doors and hardware, or aluminium systems? Already estimating, or looking to take your experience from the tools into the office?
Total Trade Constructions (TTC) is looking for a motivated Estimator to join our established Commercial Fit-Out division.
We're open to applications from both experienced commercial fit-out estimators and skilled tradespeople looking to transition into an office-based estimating career.
This is an opportunity to work directly with our Managing Director, Head of Commercial Fit-Out and experienced delivery team, pricing projects for some of Melbourne's leading commercial builders.
About TTC
Total Trade Constructions is an established Melbourne commercial subcontractor with dedicated divisions in Commercial Fit-Out and Concreting.
This position sits within our Commercial Fit-Out division, which delivers a wide range of projects across Melbourne, including commercial offices, workplace fit-outs, refurbishments, universities and education facilities.
Our specialist trade packages include:
- Steel stud framing and plasterboard partitions
- Suspended, acoustic and architectural feature ceilings
- Aluminium framing and internal glazed partition systems
- Commercial doors, frames, door hardware and associated installation works
- Commercial carpentry, internal linings and architectural finishes
- Associated commercial interior and fit-out works
We have long-standing relationships with leading Melbourne builders, a strong pipeline of tender opportunities and an experienced team delivering our projects.
We're proud of the culture we've built at TTC. We're a young, motivated and energetic team that enjoys working together, supports one another and takes pride in delivering quality projects. We have a vibrant office environment where everyone is encouraged to contribute ideas, take ownership and enjoy what they do.
The Opportunity
We're looking for someone to take ownership of our estimating and pre-construction workflow, from the moment a tender enquiry comes through to the handover of a successful project to our delivery team.
Working closely with our Managing Director and Head of Commercial Fit-Out, you'll help assess which opportunities we pursue, prepare accurate and competitive quotations and maintain strong communication with our builder clients throughout the tender process.
This is a hands-on, specialist trade-estimating position, not a general building estimator role.
You'll be pricing the work our own teams deliver, with a focus on understanding construction details, quantities, materials, labour, supplier pricing, installation methods and practical buildability.
You'll have the opportunity to take real ownership of your work, build relationships with builders and suppliers, and contribute to the continued development of our estimating systems and processes.
What You'll Be Doing
- Managing incoming tender opportunities and maintaining our CRM and estimating pipeline.
- Reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, schedules and tender documentation.
- Completing detailed quantity take-offs for partitions, ceilings, aluminium, glazing, doors, hardware and associated commercial fit-out works.
- Preparing accurate estimates covering materials, labour, plant, access requirements and project-specific costs.
- Obtaining and reviewing supplier and specialist trade quotations, including maintaining competitive material and trade pricing.
- Building and maintaining relationships with key suppliers, manufacturers and trade partners.
- Identifying scope gaps, discrepancies and risks, and submitting RFIs to builders.
- Preparing and submitting professional tender quotations, including scope qualifications and exclusions.
- Managing tender revisions, repricing, value-management options and alternative construction solutions.
- Liaising with builders, suppliers, manufacturers and our internal delivery teams throughout the tender process.
- Attending site inspections, tender meetings and project walk-throughs when required.
- Supporting builder relationships through professional communication and proactive tender follow-up.
- Preparing clear and accurate project handovers when tenders are successful.
- Helping improve TTC's estimating systems, pricing databases, templates and processes, including the use of AI and modern digital tools.
Who We're Looking For
Ideally, you'll bring experience in commercial partitions, ceilings, plastering, steel stud framing, carpentry, doors and hardware, aluminium systems or a related commercial interiors trade.
We're particularly interested in hearing from:
- Experienced Estimators: Currently working for commercial fit-out contractors or specialist trade subcontractors.
- Commercial Tradespeople: Framing carpenters, plasterers, door installers or aluminium installers with a strong understanding of plans and construction methods.
- Tradespeople Looking for a Change: Someone with a solid commercial trade background, good computer skills and an interest in transitioning from the tools into an estimating career.
- Developing Estimators: Individuals with some estimating experience who are looking to take on greater responsibility and further develop their skills.
You'll be organised, commercially minded and comfortable communicating with builders, suppliers and colleagues.
Strong computer skills and an eye for detail are essential. Experience with digital take-off software, Excel, CRM platforms and AI-assisted workflows would be advantageous.
We're looking for someone with a positive attitude, a willingness to learn and the motivation to become an important part of our team.
Previous estimating experience is highly regarded, but we're prepared to train the right person with a solid commercial trade background and the right attitude.
Why Join TTC?
- Great Team & Culture: Join a young, energetic and motivated team in a fun, vibrant and supportive office environment.
- Established Business: Be part of a respected Melbourne commercial subcontractor with strong builder relationships and consistent tender opportunities.
- Work Alongside Experienced Leaders: Work directly with our Managing Director, Head of Commercial Fit-Out and experienced delivery team.
- Genuine Career Development: Whether you're an experienced estimator or transitioning from the tools, we'll support you in developing your skills and growing with the business.
- Modern Systems & Technology: Join a business actively investing in technology, AI and smarter estimating processes, with opportunities to help shape how we work.
- Interesting Commercial Projects: Work across a variety of commercial offices, workplace fit-outs, refurbishments and education projects throughout Melbourne.
- Ownership & Responsibility: Have the opportunity to manage your own tender workload, contribute ideas and make a genuine impact on the business.
- Competitive Salary: Remuneration tailored to your trade knowledge, estimating capabilities and experience.
Ready for Your Next Move?
Whether you're already an estimator or an experienced commercial tradesperson looking to move off the tools, we'd love to hear from you.
If you understand how commercial interiors are built, enjoy solving problems, have a good attitude and want to work with a motivated team that genuinely enjoys what they do, this could be the opportunity for you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a brief outline of your relevant commercial construction or estimating experience.
Total Trade Constructions – Certainty. Delivered.

Company Description
Nacap is a leading player in the pipeline and civil works industry, and part of the Quanta Services group. Job Description
Kick-start your career protecting the land, water and environment behind some of Australia's biggest infrastructure projects. Nacap is launching a brand-new Environmental Graduate stream — and we're looking for our first intake to start January 2027. 
As an Environmental Graduate, you'll join Nacap's newest Graduate Program stream and get hands-on exposure across every part of how we protect the environment around our projects. Over an 18-month structured program, you'll complete three 6-month rotations: 
- Environmental & Approvals — Implementing the business Environmental Management System (EMS), undertaking approvals and compliance tracking, environmental reporting and providing project environmental support.  
- Site-Based Delivery — two rotations out on a live project site, putting it all into practice through field work, inspections, reporting and day to day environmental management. 
You'll be based at our Doncaster head office for the office-based rotations, with a site-based rotation (FIFO/DIDO) taking you out to where the real work happens. You'll be paired with an experienced mentor, join in-house Masterclasses, and get the support you need to build toward an Environmental Advisor role — and beyond.

- A degree (or be in your final year) in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or a related discipline. 
- Graduated within the last year, or currently in your final year of study. 
- Strong communication skills, positive approach, and the confidence to build relationships with a huge range of people — Traditional Owners, landholders, regulators and project teams alike. 
- A team-first and proactive attitude, and the willingness to get out on site (FIFO/DIDO) when your rotation calls for it. 
- Previous exposure to environmental management work (an internship, cadetship or site experience) is a bonus, not a requirement — we'll teach you the rest.

- Real responsibility, early. You'll be trusted with genuine project work from day one, not just observing from the back of the room. 
- A program built around you. Three rotations, a dedicated mentor, in-house Masterclasses and professional development support (including pathways through the Environment Institute of Australia and New Zealand) — all designed to set you up for a long career. 
- A seat at the table. You'll present your experiences directly to Nacap's Operations Leadership Group and Executive Committee — your voice counts here, from year one. 
- A genuine career path. This program is designed to take you from graduate to Environmental Advisor, with plenty of room to keep growing from there. 
- A values-driven culture. Integrity, teamwork and a relentless drive to be better aren't just words on a wall — they shape how we work, every day. 
Perks & benefits 
- Attractive salary package — we value your contribution from day one. 
- Discounts program — everyday savings at over 400 retailers. 
- Employee Assistance Program — support for your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. 
- Generous employee referral program — know a great future teammate? Earn a bonus for the introduction. 
- Flexibility and wellbeing — we understand the importance of balance. 
- Free onsite parking at our Doncaster office. 
- An outstanding, social culture — including volunteer days and a genuinely supportive team.

This is a rare chance to help shape a brand-new graduate stream at Nacap — and build a career protecting the places we build in. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

- Perform quality control inspections and material verification to ensure compliance with applicable standards and customer requirements.
- Contribute to the planning, execution, and evaluation of laboratory studies and experimental investigations.

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and perform effectively in a dynamic and changing work environment.
- A professional attitude, commitment to quality, and a customer-focused approach to laboratory services.
Preferred Technical Expertise:
Experience in the following areas will be highly regarded:
- Metallurgical testing and failure analysis.
- Chemical composition analysis and material verification.
- Macro- and microstructural examination of welds and metallic components.
- Mechanical property testing and hardness evaluation.
- Positive Material Identification (PMI) and EDX/EDS analysis.
- Destructive and non-destructive testing of engineering materials.
- Material selection, quality assurance, and compliance with relevant engineering standards.
- Preparation of technical reports and interpretation of laboratory test results.

This position offers an opportunity to contribute to a broad range of materials testing, metallurgical assessment, and engineering investigations. The successful candidate will work closely with laboratory personnel and clients to deliver technically sound, accurate, and reliable testing outcomes while maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and professionalism.
Candidates with relevant qualifications, practical laboratory experience, and a strong interest in materials testing and engineering investigations are encouraged to apply.

candidates.content_text:
Do you see opportunity everywhere in anywhere connectivity? Then come and propel your career at Myriota, where the Internet of Things (IoT) meets Space!
At Myriota our mission is audacious yet simple: unlock better outcomes for people and planet, through simple, affordable access to data. We make anywhere connectivity possible through our patented direct-to-satellite technology that is secure, low-cost, low maintenance and really (really) long-battery-life.
One more thing… It works today. This is why our solutions are profitably unlocking vital use cases across a range of industries including agriculture, environmental monitoring, transport, logistics, maritime and defence.
The incredible opportunity:
As an NPI (New Product Introduction) Engineer within our Edge team, you will act as the primary technical anchor taking complex, satellite-connected electronic hardware from R&D prototype into scaled, commercial contract manufacturing.
Reporting directly to the Electronics Lead, you will bridge the gap between engineering design and high-volume mass production. You’ll embed Design for Manufacture (DFM) and Design for Test (DFT) early in the design cycle, architect automated production test fixtures, drive factory quality frameworks, and collaborate with both local and offshore Contract Manufacturers (CMs) to ensure our direct-to-orbit edge hardware is delivered reliably, cost-effectively, and at scale.
What we’ll trust you with: 
- Leading the end-to-end technical handover of edge hardware from internal R&D to contract manufacturing partners, orchestrating prototype, pilot, and full production build gates.
- Partnering with electronics engineers early in development to evaluate schematics, PCB layouts, assembly tolerances, and component selection to maximize first-pass yield (FPY).
- Specifying, designing, and rolling out automated factory test fixtures, test software, and assembly processes that ensure 100% functional test coverage prior to deployment.
- Directing day-to-day technical engagement with local and remote CMs, defining SOPs, standard process flows, and rapidly resolving production-floor technical inquiries.
- Driving root-cause investigations on manufacturing defects using structured quality methodologies, including PFMEA, 8D analysis, and Pareto tracking to systematically eliminate scrap and line failures.
- Maintaining engineering change orders (ECOs), ensuring design integrity, and verifying requirements against strict Verification & Validation (V&V) traceability matrices.
- Leaning in with an "all hands on deck" mindset to support ad-hoc engineering challenges, alternative component sourcing, and cross-functional hardware priorities as we grow.
What we'd love to see in you: 
- Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering, Mechatronics, Process Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
- 3+ years of commercial hardware experience transitioning complex electronic products into scaled mass production.
- Hands-on experience working with both local and offshore/remote Contract Manufacturers (CMs) across trial builds and volume ramps.
- Demonstrated ability to specify, build, or implement automated manufacturing test fixtures and test regimes for electronic assemblies.
- Practical experience applying PFMEA, 8D problem solving, yield analysis, and V&V requirements traceability.
- Strong technical documentation skills with the ability to translate complex engineering constraints into clear assembly and test instructions.
- Familiarity with reviewing schematics/PCBs in CAD tools (such as Altium Designer), or exposure to embedded software (C/C++) and scripting (Python, Bash) for test automation and telemetry analysis.
- An analytical, proactive problem solver who is quality-obsessed, self-reliant, and driven by collective team success.
Why Myriota stands out:
- Driven by Purpose: Our mission creates meaningful impacts for both individuals and the planet.
- Shared Values: We embrace values that include Thinking Big, Simplifying, Collaborating, and Staying Authentic.
- Nurturing Growth: Count on tailored development plans that empower your potential. 
- Flexibility & Empowerment: We champion work-life balance, well-being, learning, and individual passions. 
- Caring Community: Our supportive culture offers mental health support, paid parental leave, birthday leave, and comprehensive health coverage. 
Our hiring commitment:
At Myriota, you don’t need to check every box.
We have key requirements which are important, but we also know that the best candidate may not tick all the boxes so, if you have the experience and capabilities for a portion of the role, Apply Now to join our energised team.
At Myriota, we're a diverse team united by strength. We warmly welcome applications from all backgrounds and walks of life. Elevate the future with us at Myriota today!
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We love hearing from candidates directly! Please note that Myriota has not engaged any external agencies for this role, and we are managing this recruitment process internally. We kindly ask that recruitment agencies respect this and refrain from cold outreach or submitting unsolicited resumes.
